messages:
lina: quick heads-up — during the high-concurrency soak (2k concurrent reqs) i saw p95 stable but p99 jumping to ~1.2s when microbatch size = 8 and kernel-fallback path triggers. looks correlated with KV cache churn :grimacing:
omar: did you repro on a single node or across the cluster?
sophie: which model/version? is this the new 30B quantized build?
lina: single dedicated host first, then across a small pool. repro with rdm-30b-q3b (prod-ish). microbatch=4 is fine, 8 triggers the tail. p50~80ms, p95~220ms, p99~1.2s.
ryan: logs? any stack traces or kernel selection lines?
lina: pasted profiler snippets below, looked like repeated kernel fallback for attention (cuda->cpu fallback path) when KV miss rate increases:
```
2026-02-15T10:33:12Z INFO kernel_selector: selected kernel=CudaOptFast
2026-02-15T10:33:12Z WARN kernel_selector: fallback=GenericAttention (reason=kv_eviction_backpressure)
2026-02-15T10:33:12Z DEBUG kv_cache: evict key=conv_849 ttl=0.0
2026-02-15T10:33:12Z DEBUG batching: microbatch_size=8 queued=12
```
hal: interesting — fallback is annotated with kv_eviction_backpressure. that suggests memory pressure triggers a slower code path. could be either locking or memcpy to CPU.
omar: do we see increased memcpy bytes or host->device stalls in nvprof?
lina: nvprof shows sporadic memcpy H2D spikes at the same timestamps. profiler flame shows attention kernel exec time low but memcpy wait large.
sophie: so path is: microbatch growth -> more active KV entries -> eviction churn -> fallback kernel that does extra host copies -> tail. makes sense.
ryan: any change in batching heuristic recently? i thought microbatch cap was adaptive based on seq length distribution.
lina: yeah, we rolled a tweak last week that raises microbatch cap when observed seq median < 128. this workload has variable prefixes so median underestimates hotset tail.
hal: sounds like two factors aligning: (1) heuristic upsized microbatch, (2) KV hotset larger than assumed -> memory pressure. result: fallback kernels + memcpy = tail spikes.
omar: repro plan? we can run controlled matrix: microbatch 2/4/8 and sim hotset size (keys per convo) 50/200/800. collect p95/p99 + memcpy time.
sophie: can we temporarily change routing to prefer kernel variant that avoids host memcpy even if a bit slower on median? might reduce p99.
ryan: +1. also add a hysteresis to microbatch upscaling: require low seq variance for 10s before bump.
lina: ran quick experiment: microbatch=4 + disable fallback -> p99 ~250ms. microbatch=8 + force non-fallback -> system OOMs on high hotset.
perf-bot: perf-regression detector: new regression flagged on 2026-02-15 10:35 for rdm-30b-q3b, delta p99 +0.9s at 2k concurrency.
hal: OK next steps: (a) rollback last microbatch heuristic tweak to previous threshold, (b) instrument kernel-selector to emit memcopy size + path tag, (c) add KV hotset metric to console and alert when > X MB, (d) run the matrix test @omar.
omar: i'll queue the matrix tonight, will attach perf traces. expected runs ~3h.
sophie: i'll prototype a kernel variant selection flag to prefer zero-host-copy paths if available, gated by per-request latency budget.
ryan: i'll prepare the hysteresis change and a canary deploy to a small pool.
lina: putting the quick mitigation in place now — scaling microbatch cap down in prod pool and enabling OOM protection on forced non-fallback. will post results in ~30m. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: deploy started: microbatch-cap-revert -> pool-prod-3 at 2026-02-15T11:05:24Z
omar: quick note — matrix job found KV hotset size of ~620 keys/convo correlates with eviction rate 0.18/s which maps to 200–500ms spikes in memcpy alone.
hal: good find. can we add a cache-adaptive microbatch limiter: if eviction_rate > threshold then reduce microbatch_target by factor 2?
sophie: yes, implement as config + runtime flag. low risk.
linA: update: after cap revert p99 dropped to ~300ms at 2k concurrency. still above baseline but much better. will follow up with traces from the matrix run.
hal: awesome. please open a short RFC for the cache-adaptive limiter and the kernel-selector memcopy telemetry. include test plan and dashboards.
ryan: adding calendar: sync Thurs 10am to review RFC + matrix results.
lina: thanks everyone — big help.
